references.text: The Egyptians forced the Israelites into hard labor with cruelty (בְּפָרֶךְ), the same word used in Leviticus 25:43 to forbid such treatment of Hebrew slaves.
Reiterates the prohibition against ruling over one's Israelite brother with harshness (בְּפָרֶךְ).
Further repetition of the prohibition against ruling with harshness over an Israelite slave, even when the owner is a foreigner.
Contains the same expression 'you shall fear your God' (וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ) as motivation for ethical conduct.
Uses the same formula 'you shall fear your God' (וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ) in connection with fair treatment of others.
The same expression 'fear your God' is used in the context of economic justice toward poor brothers.
Ezekiel criticizes shepherds who rule over the flock with harshness and severity (בְּפָרֶךְ), contrary to God's will.
Elaborates on the laws concerning the release of Hebrew slaves and reminds them of Israel's own slavery in Egypt as motivation for good treatment.
Paul urges masters to treat their slaves fairly and equally, in line with the principle that they too have a Master in heaven.
Masters are urged to refrain from threatening their slaves, because they know their Master is in heaven—a parallel to the fear of God in Leviticus.
